answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 announcing a revenue-sharing and credit-support model for AI clouds, with quotes and examples from partners, cited as incoming evidence with item records e2 to e4.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says its new model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, with AI clouds selling NVIDIA-powered cloud services and NVIDIA earning both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity. NVIDIA also says this provides a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream.
findings.use: Supports a reading of the revenue structure NVIDIA has announced for this channel: product sales plus a cloud-revenue share on supported capacity. It does not yet support a conclusion that this stream is material or that it will recur at scale.
findings.grounds: This is company disclosure from NVIDIA, which can establish the model it has designed and the revenue types it intends to earn. It cannot establish the size of the share, the contract terms, the number of AI clouds signed, or the utilization of supported capacity. The recurring characterization is NVIDIA's own framing and is not measured in the article. The main uncertainty is whether usage-linked revenue will be large enough to matter relative to product sales.
findings.next_check: Look for disclosed terms in NVIDIA filings or later announcements: revenue-share percentages, whether the share is recognized as revenue or other income, how supported capacity is defined, and whether any cloud-revenue share is reported separately from product revenue.

findings.claim: The model uses credit support to help AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure. The article says the structure is economically aligned through revenue-sharing and credit-support, and that even long-term customer commitments have been insufficient to unlock financing for compute.
findings.use: Raises a lead on a possible NVIDIA financial exposure: if NVIDIA provides credit support, it may take on contingent liabilities tied to AI cloud borrowing or lease obligations. The article does not establish that NVIDIA itself guarantees any debt.
findings.grounds: The term credit support appears in NVIDIA's own description, so it establishes that such support is part of the announced model. The article gives no amount, counterparty, guarantee form, or trigger, and it does not say whether credit support is provided by NVIDIA, by a third party, or by the AI cloud's customers. The inference that NVIDIA bears contingent risk is the analyst's premise, not something the source states.
findings.next_check: Check NVIDIA's annual and quarterly filings for guarantees, residual value commitments, loan support, purchase obligations or other off-balance-sheet arrangements linked to AI cloud partners, and check whether any such obligation is quantified and whether it is disclosed as a guarantee of third-party debt.

findings.claim: Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which NVIDIA says is expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
findings.use: Supports a conditional scenario in which a single AI cloud partner builds a very large NVIDIA-based campus. If built as described, it would indicate large potential demand for NVIDIA GPUs in that project. It does not show that Firmus has ordered these GPUs from NVIDIA or that the revenue-sharing model applies to this campus.
findings.grounds: The scale figures are forward-looking plans stated by NVIDIA in its own announcement, and the article gives no construction schedule, financing, power contract status, or purchase commitment. NVIDIA can report that the campus is planned, but the article does not show how much of the 170,000 GPUs is contracted or when they would be delivered. The main uncertainty is execution: whether the campus is built, on what timetable, and at what share of the stated maximum.
findings.next_check: Look for Firmus disclosures, Indonesian permits or power agreements, and any NVIDIA statement of GPU shipments or orders to Firmus or the Batam project, with dates and quantities. A confirmed multi-phase schedule or a named purchase agreement would strengthen the scenario; a lack of such evidence would weaken it.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says AI cloud companies are already building DSX AI factories designed to serve customers and workloads across regions.
findings.use: Supports a lead that the model is being applied in practice across several AI cloud partners. It does not establish how many factories exist, their size, or their NVIDIA purchase volume.
findings.grounds: This is an unquantified company statement about progress. NVIDIA can know which partners it works with, but the article provides no count, locations beyond the Firmus example, or spending figures. The phrase already taking shape is promotional and does not supply a dated milestone.
findings.next_check: Identify the named AI cloud partners building DSX factories, with locations, megawatt capacity, GPU counts and expected online dates, from NVIDIA or partner disclosures.

findings.claim: Sharon AI CEO James Manning says the collaboration with NVIDIA marks a pivotal moment in Sharon AI's mission to deliver sovereign, large-scale AI compute infrastructure.
findings.use: Supports only the limited conclusion that Sharon AI has publicly described a collaboration with NVIDIA on sovereign, large-scale AI compute. It does not show the terms, scale, timing or whether the revenue-sharing or credit-support model applies to Sharon AI.
findings.grounds: The speaker is the CEO of Sharon AI, so he can know the company's relationship and its strategic description. The quote is reported through NVIDIA's announcement, and its statement is qualitative. The uncertainty that matters is that the quote is positive framing and carries no measurable commitment.
findings.next_check: Look for Sharon AI's own filing or press release that names the NVIDIA agreement, its scope, capacity, and whether NVIDIA provides any financing or credit support.

findings.claim: NVIDIA names Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI as AI natives that show where compute demand is headed, saying they need immediate access to AI cloud capacity for training, post-training, fine-tuning and high-volume agentic inference.
findings.use: Raises a lead on the end-demand segment the model targets, but the article does not show that these companies are customers, partners, or beneficiaries of the NVIDIA model.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is describing the demand profile of these companies, which it may know through its ecosystem relationships. The article does not say that these companies purchase through AI clouds or that they have contracts linked to NVIDIA infrastructure. The examples are illustrative, not evidence of revenue or volume.
findings.next_check: Check whether Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI disclose purchases of AI cloud capacity powered by NVIDIA, or any agreements with NVIDIA or NVIDIA partners tied to this model, and whether their compute spend is material to any named AI cloud.
